newsitem.title: PERU: Daewoo sees Peru car sales up 43 pct.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo sees Peru car sales up 43 pct.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Motor Co Ltd hopes its income from the sale of cars imported into Peru to rise to $100 million this year, up 43 percent from 1996, a top firm executive said.
"We expect to sell about 10,000 vehicles this year, compared to 7,477 in 1996", Daewoo Peru's executive president Yeong Yeol Lee told Reuters in an interview.

Only one in 43 Peruvians has a car, compared to one out of every 4.5 South Koreans, and Lee said Daewoo hoped to help reduce the breach. He said his firm has become Peru's number one car brand after only five years on the market.
Lee said that 50 percent of its Peruvian sales this year will be for the taxi market, where its Tico model has been a success.
Daewoo is also eyeing the hotel industry, and is considering investments in Peruvian telecommunications, energy and mining.
"We will be building a five-star hotel in Lima. It could cost over $100 million to build," Lee said.
